text:
Registered residential sales reached 13,075 units in the last four weeks, totaling AED 37,744,906,472. This represents a 12.6 percent increase in volume compared to the previous four-week period. Mortgage registrations were recorded as separate transactions, totaling 5,491, and are not included in the sales count. The off-plan share of sales remained stable at 56.8 percent, slightly down from 57.2 percent in the prior period.

The median residential price per square foot rose to AED 1,734, marking a 2.7 percent increase from the previous four-week median of AED 1,688. This pricing trend aligns with the overall value growth of 10.0 percent observed in the market. The data reflects registered transactions only, excluding bulk deals and partial-share transfers that might skew averages.

Rental activity showed 107,791 Ejari contracts registered, with renewals accounting for 52.6 percent of the total. The median annual residential rent stood at AED 67,144. In terms of yields, International City Phase 1 led with an estimated gross yield of 8.7 percent for flats, followed by Zaabeel First at 7.6 percent. Town Square, Dubai Sports City, and Dubai Studio City also recorded yields above 6.0 percent.

The watch-list highlights significant divergence in community performance. Al Yufrah 1 saw the strongest 12-week price appreciation at 24.3 percent, while Saih Shuaib 1 experienced the steepest decline at 29.2 percent. Jumeirah Lakes Towers cooled by 11.9 percent, contrasting with the broader market uptick. Anomaly monitoring flagged 993 sales in the last 60 days priced more than 35 percent away from comparable medians. These figures are derived from registered DLD data and Ejari contracts, using medians and benchmark filters to exclude outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
